# canreport <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="120" alt="canreport logo" />

`canreport` provides tools for generating narrative reports from Population-Based Cancer Registry (PBCR) analysis outputs.

The package is designed to work with structured report data, such as output from `canregtools`, and supports reproducible text generation workflows for `knitr` and R Markdown reports. It helps produce standardized, consistent, and bilingual cancer registry report text from statistical results.

## Installation

canreport requires R 4.1 or later. Install the development version from GitHub:

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("gigu003/canreport")
```

From a local source checkout, run `devtools::install()` in the package root.

## Quick start

Use the bundled example tables to generate report text and inspect the
values used in each paragraph.

### Generate an incidence overview

```{r overview-example}
library(canreport)

overview <- cr_overview(
  asr,
  cancer = "Breast cancer",
  event_type = "incidence",
  area = 410000,
  lang = "en",
  output = "both"
)

cat(overview$text)
```

`output = "both"` returns the paragraph in `text`, a one-row data frame in
`data`, and a named list of template values in `values`. Select the fields
you want to review alongside the narrative:

```{r structured-output-example}
overview$data[c("year", "no_cases", "cr", "asr_cn2000", "rank")]
```

For `cr_overview()`, `cr_overview_total()`, and `cr_qua_summary()`,
`output = "text"` is the default and `output = "data"` returns the one-row
table alone.

### Describe an age-specific incidence pattern

```{r age-pattern-example}
paragraph <- cr_age_pattern(
  agerate,
  cancer = "Lung cancer",
  event_type = "incidence",
  area = 410000,
  lang = "zh"
)
cat(paragraph)
```

To include the paragraph in R Markdown, put `cat(paragraph)` in a chunk with
`results = "asis"`. In Quarto, use the chunk option `#| output: asis`.

## Choose an input table and function

| Example table | What it contains | Report functions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `asr` | Case or death counts, crude and age-standardized rates, and ranks | `cr_overview()`, `cr_overview_total()`, `cr_topn()`, `cr_spectrum()` |
| `agerate` | Counts, denominators, and rates by age group | `cr_age_pattern()`, `cr_age_pattern_total()` |
| `cr_pop` | Population counts by area, sex, and age group | `cr_coverage()` |
| `cr_quality` | Registry quality indicators such as MV%, DCO%, and M/I | `cr_qua_summary()` |
| `site_icd10`, `site_morp` | Counts by ICD-10 subsite or morphology group | `cr_subsite()` |

For your own data, prepare one analysis year and one event type per input
table before generating a paragraph. Match the columns and strata in the
corresponding example table. For instance, prepare an ASR table with
`canregtools::create_asr()` and `canregtools::add_labels()`. Overview
paragraphs use the main area's total, male, and female rows and the urban
and rural comparison rows. Use `area_roles` if your urban and rural codes
differ from the defaults of `910000` and `920000`.

Use `lang = "zh"` for Chinese and `lang = "en"` for English in the
narrative functions. Set `event_type` to match the input table's
incidence or mortality statistics. See the help page for each function
for the required columns and available arguments, for example
`?canreport::cr_overview`.

## Report templates and chapters

Narrative templates live in [`inst/templates/`](inst/templates/) and share
labels and wording from [`inst/lang/`](inst/lang/). Use
`cr_chapters("methods", lang = "en")` to retrieve the built-in methods
chapter as Markdown source. It returns the chapter with its embedded
code chunks, which run when the report containing them is rendered.
